deep.reconstruction:
Folio 53v carries no original writing by Gauss. Everything visible is mirror-image show-through from the other side of the leaf, which is the page transcribed above as the 'previous page' (53r). Read in mirror, the visible elements match that page exactly.

(a) A header line ending '= 0', which is the mirror of 'x^7 - 28.x^4 + 761,9144 + 460,69681.i = 0'. Fragments such as '761,9144' and '460,69681' can be picked out reversed.

(b) A block of 7 rows. Each row has a signed complex root a + b.i, a column log r with 'n' marks, and an angle column (degrees, minutes, seconds).

(c) A 'Summe' row and a 'log f ... phi ...' row.

(d) A second header that is the mirror of 'x^7 - 28.x^4 - 201,9144 + 460,69681.i = 0', followed by the same 7 + 2 row layout.

The row counts, column structure, signs, and visible digit groups agree with 53r. The faint 'x^3' in the machine transcription is a misreading of the mirrored 'x^7'.

So there is no derivation on this page to reconstruct. For context only, the mirrored source page (53r) does the following.
- Gauss lists the seven roots of x^7 - 28x^4 + c = 0 for complex c.
- Each root carries log10 of its modulus, with 'n' marking a negative real part. He also gives an angle S.
- As controls, the roots sum to about 0, since the x^6 coefficient is 0.
- The sum of the log-moduli equals log10|c|, called 'log f', since the product of the roots is -c.
- The 'Summe' of the angles agrees with 'phi' to within hundredths of an arc-second. The precise angle convention is not fully determinable from this page.

This belongs to his numerical study of how the roots of x^7 - 28x^4 + const move as the constant varies (cf. the next page, 'x^7 - 28.x^4 + 76,19031634 = 0', with three real roots). It is connected with his late work on the fundamental theorem of algebra and the location of roots. I recall the same polynomial family serving as an illustration in his 1849 jubilee paper, but I am unsure of that.
errors: No mathematical content of Gauss's own on this page, so there are no errors to assess. The machine transcription's 'x^3' should read 'x^7' (seen mirrored).
